title: You Can’t Get Strong Alone
paragraphs: “Take a step forward?”
“Yeah. Just like you chose to trust me and stand up for me, all you need to do is think about moving forward together when your juniors grow stronger.”
Father continues, as if to say there’s nothing difficult about it. As expected of him—he always has some useful advice to offer.
“You don’t have to overreach. Just meet them where they are and play together. That alone makes a difference. Before you know it, you’ll find yourself where you wanted to be.”
“Is… that really how it works?”
“At the start, yes. Even I began that way.”
Ren looks like he’s having trouble accepting this.
“Then why does that guy have so many comrades? No offense, but within Brave Star, I was stronger than him.”

“Hmm… Maybe it’s because he was good at looking after others? Or just sociable. MMORPGs, as the name implies, favor large groups. The more allies you have, the more help you can get. A solo player I knew used to say, ‘These guys can’t do anything unless they flock together.’”
Father gives a wry smile as he speaks to Ren.
“Was he one of the top guild members?”
“…No, but I always felt like he had more comrades than I did.”

“Might have been a case of ‘the grass is greener on the other side.’ In the end, it’s all about how much value you can provide to your allies. If you don’t have the mindset to put in the effort, it’s not something you can sustain.”

Then, with a playful grin, Father adds, “So go easy on me, okay?” A hard worker, huh… Now that I think about it, Father struggled a lot in the first world. Not just the false accusations that led to a series of hardships, but even in the village he helped establish, he was always busy. Still, people like Keel admired him, so he must have been doing something right.
“Honestly, there’s not much to be jealous of. But on the other hand, you should be careful about certain types of people.”
“Like who?”
“The ones who see others as mere stepping stones to make themselves stronger. Even if you help them out of kindness, it won’t benefit you, and it’ll only lead to bad outcomes for them as well.”
At that moment, I was sure—I was looking at Father. Does Ren know someone like that? He nods repeatedly, as if something clicked.
“I don’t know much about online games, but I’ve heard there are a lot of strange people on the internet.”
“Yeah. With so many people, you get all sorts.”
“Right. No matter how high you look, there’s always someone above you. But the same goes for looking down, too.”
That, I can understand as well. After all, I played Emerald Online too.
“Motoyasu-kun trying to power-level us has some similarities to this issue. Though, I’d like to believe we won’t fall into the same problems.”
“It’s fine! No problem at all!”
After all, we’re talking about Father and the others. They’ll surely master whatever power they obtain.
“Anyway, I don’t want you to project your friend onto me and develop an unnecessary dislike for me. We’re not here to decide who among us is the best.”
“…I get it. Now that I think about it, that guy was ruthless to anyone he considered an enemy. He’s not really someone I should be comparing to Naofumi.”
“By the way, the previous world’s Father said that Ren and Itsuki acted like they were the protagonists of the story.”
The room instantly froze. Father, Ren, and Itsuki all let out awkward chuckles.
“I won’t deny it… Yeah. I do feel like the protagonist.”
“Well, everyone is the main character of their own life, after all.”
“Apparently, people stronger than themselves either betray them or die protecting them.”
“Ah… That’s a pretty common trope in games. Yeah, that kind of thinking is extremely dangerous. In this case, it would mean Motoyasu either betrays us or dies.”
“If Motoyasu-san were destined to die due to some flaw, then we’d definitely start thinking of ourselves as the protagonists.”
“So all I have to do is survive until the end?”
“That’s not how logic works! Damn it… Motoyasu, you’re ruining the mood!” Ren says with obvious irritation.
Hmm, I don’t think that’s true, though.

“Anyway, if you want to hear about guild management experience or anything like that, I’m happy to share. It’s not like we need to keep secrets from each other. Besides, in the end, Ren might end up being more respected than I am.”
“Yeah… Maybe if I watch how Naofumi handles his companions, I’ll start to understand. He was apparently really skilled at it in the future.”
“I’ll do my best so I can teach you. We’re all taking a step forward.”
“Got it. But… aren’t you kind of treating me like a kid?”
What is he saying? That’s only natural. Ren is a high school student, and Father is a college student. From a college student’s perspective, a high schooler is basically a kid.
“Ah… Sorry, I didn’t mean it that way. It’s just that you’re close in age to my younger brother, so I might have subconsciously treated you like him.”
“You have a younger brother, Naofumi?”
“Yeah. A younger brother who’s better than his older brother. He’s a senior in high school, so technically, he’s closer to Itsuki in age. When we were little, I used to take care of him a lot.”
“Huh. What kind of person is he?”
“Well… He went through a delinquent phase, got obsessed with dating sims, cared way too much about appearances, always made me cook for him… Honestly, he’s a bit of an oddball, for better or worse.”
“Sounds like he has a serious bro-con complex.”
“Who knows? But he’s smart, does well in school, and even has a girlfriend, so I have to give him credit for that.”
At that moment, Father suddenly seemed to recall something.
“Now that I think about it… My brother does kendo, and he once said that no matter how much he practiced alone, he couldn’t get any stronger. Maybe the same applies to games.”
“…That might be true. If the opportunity arises, I guess I’ll try adapting to others… if that’s the fastest way to improve.”
Yes, yes, that was a good conversation. Now then… I turn to Itsuki. As soon as I shift my gaze, Itsuki raises an eyebrow slightly.
“Well then, next is Itsuki’s issue.”
“Don’t turn the conversation onto me now!”
At Itsuki’s words, both Ren and Father give wry smiles. And before I can say anything else, Ren speaks up.
“So, in quests, you played the role of a champion of justice? And you ended up creating more trouble because your solutions were incomplete?”
“It’s the vice-shogun playstyle, I say. In the first world, Father called it a religion.”

“Well… If you keep solving various incidents, people will start believing in you like followers, won’t they? The results might have been bad, but trying to do the right thing isn’t a bad thing in itself.”
“The problem is that their allies start mistaking themselves for some privileged class and become tyrannical.”

“Right, just being a Hero comes with a certain amount of authority, doesn’t it? So it makes sense that they’d get the wrong idea. It seems like things took a turn for the worse, just in a different direction than Ren’s group.”
“Naofumi-san, I’m sure you understand this, but—”
“Yeah, we could easily end up in the same situation. We just have to be careful. Honestly… just look at Motoyasu.”
At Father’s words, Ren and Itsuki turn to look at me. Then they start nodding.
“What is it?”
“Ah… yeah, I get it.”
“Yeah. No doubt about it—he’s practically one of Naofumi’s future followers.”
Father and the others nod with half-lidded eyes. What exactly do they mean by that?
“But doesn’t it seem like he wasn’t treated all that well? At least from what I’ve heard about Naofumi’s story from the first world.”
“Yeah. He was acting for the sake of that girl, Filo, right? It really feels like he was just trying to stay in her good graces.”
“No doubt about it. And after that, he probably started acting for Naofumi-san’s sake instead, in Filo’s place.”
“I came to understand the truth and was deeply moved by Father’s vast generosity, I say!”

After all, the great Filolials, as well as many other people, believe in Father. It was not Ren, Itsuki, or myself who solved numerous problems—it was Father. So to say that I was only trying to please Filo-tan is truly an insult. I, Motoyasu, simply wish to be believed in on this one matter.
“Alright, alright, calm down.”
“Well, Naofumi-san is the Shield Hero, and different people have different strengths and weaknesses. I think it would be good if he could use his experience to support Motoyasu-san.”
“You’re subtly trying to push Motoyasu onto me, aren’t you? …Well, whatever.”
“We leave it to you, Naofumi.”
“Yeah, yeah. Geez, this is the only time you guys actually trust me, huh?”
I feel like Father and the others just strengthened their bond even further.
“In the end, we’re just people who were chosen by special weapons. If we keep that in mind and act within reason, things should be fine.”
“Simple, but true.”
“Yeah. This world isn’t a game. Just because we’re strong doesn’t mean we can do whatever we want.”
“Exactly. Being strong doesn’t justify killing indiscriminately.”
Father and the others exchange firm nods. They’ve been doing that a lot, haven’t they?
“Motoyasu-kun, you can’t just rely on strength to solve everything, alright?”
“Understood!”

I salute, taking Father’s words to heart. That said, there are plenty of things that must be resolved with strength, aren’t there? But I’ll keep that to myself. As future Father once said: “Only bring things to the negotiating table after you’ve stripped the other side of their will to fight.”
And so, our first lesson on strengthening methods came to an end, and we went to sleep.
